questions.question: Which statement is the strongest invariant for a seat-reservation system?
options: Use a cache to make the seat map faster.
A seat may be confirmed for at most one buyer for a show.
The system should use microservices.
Notifications should be sent within one minute.
questions.explanation: An invariant is a fact that must remain true despite concurrency, retries, or failures. The other choices are design options or service targets.

questions.question: A product has 1.2 million daily active users, eight actions per user per day, and a 45x peak factor. About how many peak actions per second should you plan around?
options: 125 QPS
questions.explanation: Average demand is 1,200,000 x 8 / 86,400, or about 111 actions per second. Multiplying by 45 gives about 5,000 peak actions per second.

questions.question: Why should a notification queue normally follow a committed reservation write?
options: It makes the database eventually consistent.
It allows the side effect to be retried without claiming success before the authoritative state exists.
It removes the need for idempotency keys.
It guarantees that all reads are cache hits.
questions.explanation: The durable reservation is the source of truth. A queue separates a retryable side effect from that commit, but still requires idempotent consumers.

questions.question: A tracking view can tolerate a location that is a few seconds old. Which response best communicates the resulting trade-off?
options: Serve the last known location with its update time and use an asynchronous materialized view.
Require strong consistency for every map refresh and omit failure behavior.
Store location only in a browser cache.
Use a queue before accepting courier updates, with no durable source of truth.
questions.explanation: Eventual reads can be acceptable when freshness is made visible. The design still needs a durable, delivery-keyed source of truth for updates.

questions.question: What makes a component unexplained in an interview design?
options: It has a well-known product name.
It appears on the diagram but has no named requirement, scale pressure, or failure it addresses.
It is placed after the API gateway.
It has more than one replica.
questions.explanation: Every major component should earn its complexity by addressing a stated constraint. Familiarity is not a justification.

questions.question: Which close-out is most useful after describing the high-level architecture?
options: Add more infrastructure services until time expires.
Repeat the technology names without discussing behavior.
Name a failure response, an observable metric, and the scale trigger for the next redesign.
Claim the design handles all future requirements.
questions.explanation: A mature answer makes its operational assumptions testable and states when the current design is no longer sufficient.
